blocks.x: On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more. This time, we ask: where was Tenzing filmed?

Jennifer Peedom first visited the Himalayas over 20 years ago as an aspiring filmmaker, tagging along with a friend who was working on an Everest expedition. One opportunity led to another and she began working as a camera operator, where she observed the huge amount of work done by Sherpas—and their disproportionate share of the risk in helping foreigners reach the summit. “This so often ends up on the cutting room floor,” Jennifer says. “Which motivated the documentary I made in 2015 called Sherpa.” Through this very film—and the relationships built in local communities as a result—came the idea to tell the story of Himalayan climber Tenzing Norgay. “I always wondered why no one had told an Everest expedition story from a Sherpa’s point of view.”

“Some of the most impactful people live in the dip of society,” says Tibetan actor Genden Phuntsok, who plays the film's namesake, Himalayan climber Tenzing Norgay. “There aren’t many stories about what Sherpas did before the mountaineers.” In Tenzing, Peedom looks at the first ascent of Everest through the lens of Tenzing, who summited alongside New Zealand mountaineer Sir Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) after persuading Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) to give him a place on the British climbing team.

“Tenzing—as did Hillary— pushed the boundaries of what was imaginable,” says Hiddleston. “What the pair’s friendship can teach us is that there is strength in human fellowship. You begin as outsiders with different frames of reference, but we're more united by the things we share. Tenzing came from the higher Tibetan plateau, Hillary from New Zealand. They shared a love and respect for the mountains—and recognized each other.”

Condé Nast Traveler sat down with Phuntsok, Peedom, and Hiddleston to discuss recreating Everest’s summit in New Zealand, filming a nail-biting sequence in a seemingly bottomless crevasse, and the power of being an outsider in a team setting.

blocks.x: Mustang, Nepal was the filming location for Tenzing's early years on the Tibetan plateau

The team spent three months in Nepal during pre-production, then shot for six weeks before heading to New Zealand. “Tenzing was born on the high Tibetan plateau, which is now China,” Peedom says. “We shot in Mustang, near the Tibetan border, for scenes showing Tenzing’s early life. The villages up there doubled beautifully for Sherpa communities, which we'd originally thought to shoot in the Khumbu region, [but the earthquakes prevented this]."

Ensuring cultural accuracy was key. “We had to check carefully because there are still sensitivities,” Peedom says. “There’s push and pull about Tenzing's identity—[not a ‘born Sherpa,’ as we see in the film]—and who he belonged to. We needed sign-off from his family to get the facts right.”

Peedom spoke to friends of Tenzing’s, who told stories of him training up the hills of Darjeeling, with rocks in his backpack. “I met Tenzing’s grandson in Australia before meeting his sons in 2003 in New Zealand, at the same event where I met Edmund Hillary,” Peedom says. “I went up to Darjeeling a couple of times when I was making Sherpa and the stories Pem Pem [Tenzing's daughter] shared about her father found their way into the fabric of the story. Then people throughout the community joined us as language and cultural consultants. The film was a sum total of 23 years of relationship building that enabled those doors to open.”

blocks.x: Tom Hiddleston, Genden Phuntsok, and Willem Dafoe in Kathmandu

When asked about shooting challenges, Peedom laughs—they did, after all, shoot at a UNESCO World Heritage Site. “Patan Durbar Square [city centre in Yala] is an active place of worship and ritual for thousands of people,” she says. “We managed to carve out two hours to shoot two major scenes, and with a huge amount of extras.” The team also shot in real monasteries: “Getting around various religious holidays and finding days to work together, these were challenges from our first day of shooting.”
